driving_question: The "hell as a corrupted file" frame: an artifact with no reader, a format whose spec was lost, corruption as a state of being rather than damage. In the digital-occult corpus, is unreadability a form of damnation — does the unreadable file occupy hell, and does the archivist who keeps re-indexing corrupted material perform a kind of exorcism, or a kind of torture?
best_collision: c02067 vs c02063 (Hayles) @0.5552 complicates: Hayles resurrects the pattern and concedes the corpse (file saved as grammar, not corpse); Soulellis makes the corpse a print job — sell the Library of the Printed Web and order it again in days — so the pattern is a live URL. Opposite answers to the same question: which side is expendable?
quote: I could sell the Library of the Printed Web and then order it again and have it delivered to me in a matter of days. (p.31)
mutation_note: The 4chan frame asked exorcism or torture; the zine answers re-PRINTING. Hell is not the unreadable file — hell is the file whose spec died, and this archive's spec is the web itself, churning daily. The damned file is not the corrupted one; it is the one the spec's own machinery deletes without noticing. The corpse here is a print job. The ghost is a live URL. Both are cheap. Only the spec-less copy is unrepeatable.
